items.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
items.fuel_detail: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, Nomex, Ultem, PMMA slabs and spheres, paraffin and Japan wax candles
hardware: Small flow duct (76 mm x 76 mm) with variable-speed fan
items.objective: Bridge the gap between the normal-gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 and real material flammability in microgravity, and test an inert gaseous extinguishing agent on different materials and geometries
items.variables: Material, sample shape (flat, sphere, cylinder, wake flames), flow direction (opposed or concurrent) and flow speed up to 40 cm/s
items.earth_application: Models apply to many terrestrial combustion problems (PSI)
items.relevance_note: PSI says current NASA spacecraft materials selection uses a 1-g test; BASS checks it in microgravity

items.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
items.fuel_detail: PMMA films, slabs and rods (0.1 to 5 mm thick), Nomex III fabric, SIBAL fabric, Japan wax candle
hardware: Small wind tunnel (flow up to 40 cm/s)
items.objective: Ignition, flame growth, flame spread and extinction limits of solid fuels in low-speed forced flow in microgravity
items.variables: Flow speed and direction; ambient oxygen (lowered below 21% by adding nitrogen); sample geometry (rods, spherical sections, slabs, films, fabric)
items.earth_application: Feeds models used to design fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Oxygen range is the calibrated initial O2 per test from the PSI experimental table

items.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment I
items.fuel_detail: SIBAL fabric (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass), about 0.94 m x 0.4 m
hardware: Saffire flow duct in the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS
sensors: Solid-state pressure, CO2 and O2 sensors
items.objective: How fast a large fire grows in low gravity, and low-g flammability limits compared with NASA's normal-gravity screening test
items.variables: Flow direction (concurrent or opposed); same material and flow speed
items.relevance_note: Large-scale fire on an exploration vehicle without risk to a crew (PSI)

items.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment II
items.fuel_detail: Nine 5 cm x 29 cm samples: silicone, SIBAL fabric, PMMA (flat and structured), PMMA with Nomex
hardware: Saffire flow duct in the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS
sensors: Solid-state pressure, CO2 and O2 sensors
items.objective: How fast a large fire grows in low gravity, and low-g flammability limits compared with NASA's normal-gravity screening test
items.variables: Material and thickness, flow direction; flow 20 cm/s in the PSI table (the PSI text also mentions 30 cm/s for some samples)
items.relevance_note: Oxygen is derived from measured CO2 and the initial ISS O2 (PSI table note)

items.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment III
items.fuel_detail: SIBAL fabric, 94 cm x 40.6 cm
hardware: Saffire flow duct in the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS
sensors: Solid-state pressure, CO2 and O2 sensors
items.objective: How fast a large fire grows in low gravity, and low-g flammability limits compared with NASA's normal-gravity screening test
items.variables: Flow direction (concurrent or opposed) at 30 cm/s, compared with 20 cm/s in Saffire-I
items.relevance_note: Same material as Saffire-I at a higher flow speed

items.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
items.fuel_detail: Overheated (not burning) spacecraft materials: Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, lampwick, dibutyl phthalate
sensors: Thermophoretic smoke samplers (analysed by electron microscope)
items.objective: Measure the size of smoke particles made in low gravity and how they affect smoke detectors
items.variables: Sample material, sample heating, air flow (5 or 10 cm/s) and smoke aging time
items.earth_application: Smoke detectors for other extreme places on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Basis for an advanced fire detector for future long-duration spacecraft (PSI)

items.name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Reflight
items.fuel_detail: Overheated (not burning) materials: Kapton, silicone, lampwick, Teflon, Pyrell fire-retardant foam
items.objective: Repeat SAME with new materials and wider conditions to measure smoke particle size in low gravity
items.variables: Material, higher heating temperatures, no-flow heating, aging time; 66 test points
items.earth_application: Smoke detectors for other extreme places on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Basis for an advanced fire detector for future long-duration spacecraft (PSI)

items.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
items.fuel_detail: No fuel: Arizona Road Dust mixed with nitrogen as a test aerosol
items.objective: Show that a P-Trak particle counter, modified for microgravity, counts aerosols correctly before it was used in SAME
items.variables: Instrument (P-Trak or DustTrak) and sampling location
items.earth_application: Instruments for other hard places on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories (PSI)
items.relevance_note: PSI keeps DAFT and DAFT-2 in one record (PSI-47); fields are shared

items.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test 2
items.fuel_detail: No fuel: Arizona Road Dust mixed with nitrogen as a test aerosol
items.objective: Show that a P-Trak particle counter, modified for microgravity, counts aerosols correctly before it was used in SAME
items.variables: Instrument (P-Trak or DustTrak) and sampling location
items.earth_application: Instruments for other hard places on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories (PSI)
items.relevance_note: PSI keeps DAFT and DAFT-2 in one record (PSI-47); fields are shared

items.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
items.fuel_detail: Methanol and heptane droplets (1.1 to 4.67 mm initial diameter)
items.objective: Map flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity and measure how well gaseous suppressants (CO2, helium) work
items.variables: Fuel, droplet size, ambient pressure, oxygen, and added CO2 or helium
items.earth_application: Fire safety in confined spaces on Earth (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Finds the lowest oxygen that still burns at each pressure (PSI)

items.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
items.fuel_detail: Droplets of iso-octane, n-octane, heptane, decane, ethanol and mixtures (1.5 to 5 mm)
items.objective: Extend FLEX to fuels and conditions like real combustors, with benchmark data on two-component droplets
items.variables: Fuel, gas mixture (O2 with nitrogen or helium), pressure, droplet size, droplet speed, droplet spacing
items.relevance_note: Flow is the speed of a moving droplet, not room airflow

items.name: Cool Flames Investigation
items.fuel_detail: n-dodecane droplets and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures
items.objective: Cool-flame burning of n-dodecane and mixtures at different pressures and helium dilution
items.variables: Pressure (0.5 to 5 atm), oxygen, helium dilution, fuel mixture, fiber-supported or free droplet
items.earth_application: Understanding of fuel octane and cetane numbers in engines (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Fundamental study; PSI says it supports the design of safer spacecraft systems

items.name: Burning Rate Emulator
items.fuel_detail: Ethylene or methane (pure or 50% in nitrogen) through 25 or 50 mm porous burners, emulating burning solids
items.objective: Burning conditions of materials in still microgravity air, as a function of material properties
items.variables: Fuel, burner size, oxygen (21 to 40%) and pressure; planned crew atmospheres: 21% O2 at 14.7 psia, 26.5% at 10.2 psia, 34% at 8.2 psia
items.relevance_note: Flames kept burning without airflow in elevated-oxygen atmospheres considered for future spacecraft; at 21% they self-extinguished (PSI). Pressure per test is not listed

items.name: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
items.fuel_detail: Ethane, propane and butane on a spherical porous burner, normal and inverse (oxygen from the burner) flames
items.objective: Conditions for steady cool diffusion flames with gaseous fuels, including inverse flames
items.variables: Fuel, dilution, flow rate, pressure, normal or inverse flame
items.relevance_note: Oxygen up to 85% is the burner flow in inverse flames; normal flames burned in 18 to 40% O2 ambient

items.name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
items.fuel_detail: Methane and ethylene (pure or diluted with nitrogen) on a coflow or gas-jet burner
items.objective: How an electric field (up to 10 kV) changes flame stability, soot and ion current in microgravity
items.variables: Field strength and polarity, fuel and dilution, burner type, coflow velocity
items.earth_application: Electric fields could reduce pollutants from combustion on Earth (PSI)
items.relevance_note: The challenge text describes it as a partial-gravity proxy

items.name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
items.fuel_detail: Methane, ethylene, propane, propylene and propylene mixtures; burners 0.41, 0.76 and 1.6 mm
items.objective: Smoke point (when a flame starts to release soot) of jet flames in co-flowing air in microgravity
items.variables: Fuel, burner diameter, co-flow air speed, fuel flow; 526 flames
items.relevance_note: PSI says it helps design safer spacecraft environments (soot)

items.name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
items.fuel_detail: Methane, ethylene and ethane, pure or diluted with nitrogen
items.objective: Structure and stability (liftoff) of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity
items.variables: Fuel and nitrogen dilution, burner diameter, coflow velocity; 13 test days
items.earth_application: Better models for more efficient combustion on Earth (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Hardware is from the challenge text; PSI leaves it blank

items.name: Flame Design
items.fuel_detail: Ethylene and propane on a spherical porous burner, normal and inverse (oxygen from the burner) flames
items.objective: Soot-inception and extinction limits of normal and inverse spherical flames
items.variables: Flow rate, fuel dilution with nitrogen, oxygen, pressure, normal or inverse flame
items.earth_application: More efficient, cleaner combustors on Earth (PSI)
items.relevance_note: Not named in the challenge; added from PSI. Oxygen up to 85% is the burner flow in inverse flames

items.name: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
items.fuel_detail: Methane and ethylene, diluted with nitrogen
items.objective: Weak coflow flames and soot at extreme fuel dilution, to test computer models
items.variables: Fuel, fuel dilution, flow velocity
items.relevance_note: Not named in the challenge; added from PSI

items.name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
items.fuel_detail: Hydrogen, methane and ethylene mixtures diluted with nitrogen or helium, on a spherical porous burner
items.objective: Structure, extinction limits and pulsating instabilities of spherical flames
items.variables: Fuel mixture, diluent (nitrogen or helium), oxygen (about 21 or 30%), flow rate
items.relevance_note: Not named in the challenge; added from PSI. Oxygen values are approximate (~) in the PSI table
